arxiv-1709-10308.title: Future prospects for exploring present day anomalies in flavour physics measurements with Belle II and LHCb
arxiv-1709-10308.creator: J. Albrecht, F. U. Bernlochner, M. Kenzie, S. Reichert, D. M. Straub, A. Tully
arxiv-1709-10308.description: Abstract A range of flavour physics observables show tensions with their corresponding Standard Model expectations: measurements of leptonic flavour-changing neutral current processes and ratios of semi-leptonic branching fractions involving different generations of leptons show deviations of the order of four standard deviations. If confirmed, either would be an intriguing sign of new physics.

arxiv-2104-00563.title: Latent Variable Sequential Set Transformers for Joint Multi-Agent Motion Prediction
arxiv-2104-00563.creator: Roger Girgis Florian Golemo Felipe Codevilla Martin Weiss, Jim Aldon D’Souza Samira E. Kahou Felix Heide Christopher Pal
arxiv-2104-00563.description: Abstract Robust multi-agent trajectory prediction is essential for the safe control of robotic systems. A major challenge is to efficiently learn a representation that approximates the true joint distribution of contextual, social, and temporal information to enable planning. We propose Latent Variable Sequential Set Transformers which are encoder-decoder architectures that generate scene-consistent multi-agent trajectories.

arxiv-2105-06443.title: Energy stability of plane Couette and Poiseuille flows and Couette paradox
arxiv-2105-06443.creator: Paolo Falsaperla, Giuseppe Mulone & Carla Perrone
arxiv-2105-06443.description: Abstract We study the nonlinear stability of plane Couette and Poiseuille flows with the Lyapunov second method by using the classical L 2 L_{2} -energy. We prove that the streamwise perturbations are L 2 L_{2} -energy stable for any Reynolds number.

arxiv-2112-06256.title: Stabilization of Microbial Communities by Responsive Phenotypic Switching
arxiv-2112-06256.creator: Pierre A. Haas, Maria A. Gutierrez, Nuno M. Oliveira, Raymond E. Goldstein
arxiv-2112-06256.description: Abstract Clonal microbes can switch between different phenotypes and recent theoretical work has shown that stochastic switching between these subpopulations can stabilize microbial communities. This phenotypic switching need not be stochastic, however, but could also be in response to environmental factors, both biotic and abiotic.

arxiv-2307-11582.title: Exploring Solar Neutrino Oscillation Parameters with LSC at Yemilab and JUNO
arxiv-2307-11582.creator: Pouya Bakhti 1, Meshkat Rajaee 1, Seon-Hee Seo 2, Seodong Shin 1,3
arxiv-2307-11582.description: Abstract We investigate the sensitivities of the liquid scintillator counter (LSC) at Yemilab and JUNO to solar neutrino oscillation parameters, focusing on θ 12 \theta_{12} and Δ ​ m 21 2 \Delta m^{2}_{21} . We compare the potential of JUNO with LSC at Yemilab utilizing both reactor and solar data in determining those parameters.

arxiv-2402-17036.title: Iterated INLA for State and Parameter Estimation in Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2402-17036.creator: Rafael Anderka, Marc Peter Deisenroth, So Takao
arxiv-2402-17036.description: Abstract Data assimilation (DA) methods use priors arising from differential equations to robustly interpolate and extrapolate data. Popular techniques such as ensemble methods that handle high-dimensional, nonlinear PDE priors focus mostly on state estimation, however can have difficulty learning the parameters accurately.

arxiv-2410-16041.title: GFlowNets for Hamiltonian decomposition in groups of compatible operators
arxiv-2410-16041.creator: Isaac L. Huidobro-Meezs, Jun Dai, Guillaume Rabusseau, Rodrigo A. Vargas-Hernández *
arxiv-2410-16041.description: Abstract Quantum computing presents a promising alternative for the direct simulation of quantum systems with the potential to explore chemical problems beyond the capabilities of classical methods. However, current quantum algorithms are constrained by hardware limitations and the increased number of measurements required to achieve chemical accuracy.

arxiv-2411-10723.title: Performance Analysis and Power Allocation for Massive MIMO ISAC Systems Thanks: This work was supported in part by the Research Council of Finland through the 6G Flagship program (grant number 369116), project DIRECTION (grant number 354901), and project FunISAC (grant 359093), by CHIST-ERA through
arxiv-2411-10723.creator: Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Van-Dinh Nguyen, Hieu V. Nguyen
arxiv-2411-10723.description: Abstract Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is envisioned as a key feature in future wireless communications networks. Its integration with massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) techniques promises to leverage substantial spatial beamforming gains for both functionalities. In this work, we consider a massive MIMO-ISAC system employing a uniform planar array with zero-forcing and maximum-ratio downlink transmission schemes combined with monostatic radar-type sensing.

arxiv-2502-01988.title: ReMiDi: Reconstruction of Microstructure Using a Differentiable Diffusion MRI Simulator
arxiv-2502-01988.creator: Prathamesh Pradeep Khole, Zahra Kais Petiwala, Shri Prathaa Magesh, Ehsan Mirafzali, Utkarsh Gupta, Jing-Rebecca Li, Andrada Ianus, Razvan Marinescu
arxiv-2502-01988.description: Abstract We propose ReMiDi, a novel method for inferring neuronal microstructure as arbitrary 3D meshes using a differentiable diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (dMRI) simulator. We first implemented in PyTorch a differentiable dMRI simulator that simulates the forward diffusion process using a finite-element method on an input 3D microstructure mesh.

arxiv-2503-10617.title: Compositional Subspace Representation Fine-tuning for Adaptive Large Language Models
arxiv-2503-10617.creator: Andy Zhou
arxiv-2503-10617.description: Abstract Adapting large language models to multiple tasks can cause cross-skill interference, where improvements for one skill degrade another. While methods such as LoRA impose orthogonality constraints at the weight level, they do not fully address interference in hidden-state representations.

arxiv-2503-18815.title: On two families of iterative methods without memory
arxiv-2503-18815.creator: Anna Cima, Armengol Gasull, Víctor Mañosa, Francesc Mañosas
arxiv-2503-18815.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anna Cima, Armengol Gasull, Víctor Mañosa, Francesc Mañosas. We study two natural families of methods of order n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 that are useful for solving numerically one variable equations f ⁡ ( x ) = 0 .

arxiv-2505-13210.title: Picturized and Recited with Dialects: A Multimodal Chinese Representation Framework for Sentiment Analysis of Classical Chinese Poetry
arxiv-2505-13210.creator: Xiaocong Du, Haoyu Pei, Haipeng Zhang
arxiv-2505-13210.description: Abstract Classical Chinese poetry is a vital and enduring part of Chinese literature, conveying profound emotional resonance. Existing studies analyze sentiment based on textual meanings, overlooking the unique rhythmic and visual features inherent in poetry, especially since it is often recited and accompanied by Chinese paintings.

arxiv-2509-14336.title: Stress Response of Jammed Solids: Prestress and Screening
arxiv-2509-14336.creator: Surajit Chakraborty, Jishnu N. Nampoothiri, Subhro Bhattacharjee, Bulbul Chakraborty, Kabir Ramola
arxiv-2509-14336.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Surajit Chakraborty, Jishnu N. Nampoothiri, Subhro Bhattacharjee, Bulbul Chakraborty, Kabir Ramola. Unlike classical elasticity, where stresses arise from deformations relative to a stress-free reference configuration, rigidity in amorphous systems is maintained by disordered force networks that generate internal prestress. Previously, we introduced a “stress-only” formulation, where mechanical equilibrium resembles Gauss’s law in a rank-2 tensor electrostatics with vector charges, and demonstrated that the mechanical response of jammed solids is described by the dielectric response of this gauge-theoretic formulation.

arxiv-2602-07839.title: TodoEvolve: Learning to Architect Agent Planning Systems
arxiv-2602-07839.description: Abstract Planning has become a central capability for contemporary agent systems in navigating complex, long-horizon tasks, yet existing approaches predominantly rely on fixed, hand-crafted planning structures that lack the flexibility to adapt to the structural diversity of open-ended problems. To address this limitation, we introduce TodoEvolve , a meta-planning paradigm that autonomously synthesizes and dynamically revises task-specific planning architectures.

We aimed to evaluate the impact of key study design factors (including confounders, applied exposure model, population age, and outcome definition) on PM2.

pmc-11642040.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure and Its Implications on Real-Time Hemodynamic Regulation, Baroreceptor Reflex Sensitivity, and Survival
pmc-11642040.creator: Anna S. Lang-Stöberl, Hannah Fabikan, Maria Ruis, Sherwin Asadi, Julie Krainer, Oliver Illini, Arschang Valipour
pmc-11642040.description: Background: Impairment in autonomic activity is a prognostic marker in patients with heart failure (HF), and its involvement has been suggested in cardiovascular complications of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) and Cheyne–Stokes respiration (CSR). This prospective observational study aims to investigate the implications of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) on hemodynamic regulation and autonomic activity in chronic HF patients.

pmc-12379293.title: A hybrid method combining rule-based filter and machine learning to detect porpoise and vessel sounds from a pulse event recorder
pmc-12379293.creator: Mayu I. Ogawa, Satoko S. Kimura, Nozomu Ishiai, Tomonari Akamatsu
pmc-12379293.description: Passive acoustic monitoring is essential for assessing the impact of anthropogenic noise on marine ecosystems and detecting vocalizing marine life. While acoustic event recorders are widely used to record odontocete echolocation due to their low power and memory demands, conventional detection algorithms are often unsuitable for analyzing datasets composed of complex pulse events.

pmc-12768633.title: PP57 Proposal For Adaptation Of The Pharmaceutical Innovativeness Index Based On Lenacapavir
pmc-12768633.creator: Alex Martins, Ludmila Gargano, Francisco Acurcio, Juliana Alvares-Teodoro, Augusto Guerra
pmc-12768633.description: IntroductionTreatment of HIV-1 infection is based on antiretroviral therapy. A pharmaceutical innovativeness index (PII) was proposed as a tool to evaluate the degree of innovativeness of technologies, initially for cancer treatment. This study aimed to adapt the PII for assessing therapies used in the treatment of people living with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 (MDR-HIV), based on an assessment of lenacapavir.

pmc-13389417.creator: M D Palmer, J Savage, P D Bates, J Neal
pmc-13389417.description: The latest Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change assessment report highlighted the potential for more than 15 m of global sea-level rise by 2300.
